_meta.simulation_note: Account and opportunity data advanced to 2026-08-10. New closes in the window: Corinthia Bank (Jul 2, $220K — 3rd ATLAS enterprise GA customer), VantagePoint renewal (Jul 15, $1.8M). Kestrel tranche 1 ($800K) released Jul 15. The dominant commercial event of the window is DR-014 (Jul 22): the SOC 2 board mandate was restated as audit-readiness Aug 31 with the Type II report at Dec 15. Every SOC 2-gated deal note has been re-baselined against Dec 15 — Nuvera moved to Q4 as a direct result. HORIZON soft GA delivered Jul 31 on time, which repaired the Solaris expectation gap; the Aug 31 public GA now rides on an Apple review decision expected Aug 15-22. Full event ledger: 1-inputs-triggers/simulation-log.json.

summary.arr_new_closed_ytd_breakdown: Brightpath $1.2M (May 1) + Apex Health $360K (Jun 16) + Finex Capital $140K (Jun 22) + Corinthia Bank $220K (Jul 2). Renewals: VantagePoint $1.8M (Jul 15).
summary.changeNote: Pipeline reduced $44.8M → $42.8M as VantagePoint ($1.8M) and Corinthia ($220K) closed. Revenue at risk fell $4.2M in the window and is now $2.4M BELOW the baseline — driven by ATLAS GA proving out, HORIZON soft GA landing on time, and SHIELD reaching 100 controls. Offsetting that: the SOC 2 date restatement (DR-014) pushed certification-gated revenue from Q3 to Q4, which is a timing loss rather than a risk increase. Active focus: Meridian Financial ($4.2M, Q4), Nuvera ($2.1M, moved to Q4), Solaris ($2.4M, Sep 15, gated on Apple), Kestrel tranche 2 ($800K, Oct).

accounts.name: Meridian Financial Group
accounts.notes: Largest active pipeline deal. Legal's 90-day clause satisfied — SOC 2 was in progress well before May 1. SHIELD hit 100/100 controls Jul 15 and Deloitte accepted the full evidence package Aug 7. Dmitri Volkov walked Yvonne Tran through DR-014 on Jul 27: audit-readiness Aug 31, observation Sep 1 – Nov 30, Type II report Dec 15. Yvonne's response was that the clarity helps more than the earlier date did — her own legal team had assumed a report, not a readiness milestone. Close moved Q3 → Q4 to sit behind the Dec 15 report. Databricks evaluation still in play.

accounts.name: Apex Health Systems
accounts.notes: CLOSED WON Jun 16 as first ATLAS enterprise GA customer. $360K initial annual contract. Live in production through the July uptime dip — Marcus Webb was notified proactively on Jul 6 when rolling uptime fell to 96.8%, and again Aug 3 when the circuit breaker restored 98.9%. Priya Shah reports the proactive disclosure strengthened the relationship rather than damaging it. Expansion potential $3.8M now gated on the Dec 15 Type II report per DR-014, not Aug 31.

accounts.name: Solaris Logistics
accounts.notes: Expectation gap RESOLVED. Jennifer Wu briefed Tom Okafor Jul 1 before beta onboarding that Jul 31 meant limited enterprise release, not App Store GA. Solaris onboarded into the beta cohort Jul 16 and soft GA landed on time Jul 31 — delivering exactly what was promised, after two prior slipped dates, materially repaired credibility. Remaining dependency: public App Store GA Aug 31, which now rides on an Apple review decision expected Aug 15-22. Tom has been told this is outside NovaGrid's control.

accounts.name: Nuvera Insurance
accounts.notes: Pilot continuing, but the close date moved. Rajiv Patel asked Sarah James directly on Jul 28 whether SOC 2 certification would be in hand on Aug 31. The honest answer under DR-014 is no — readiness Aug 31, report Dec 15. Rajiv's Q3 board deadline cannot be met with a readiness statement, so the close moved to Q4 behind the Dec 15 report. Sarah's assessment: the deal is not lost and the champion is intact, but this is the clearest commercial cost of the date restatement. ATLAS GA and 100/100 controls both remain strong signals.

Elena Markov's Sep 15 roadmap review is contractual and expects SPARK M2 (model serving alpha) to have closed. M2 is at 88% against an Aug 11 target, so the review is live but not yet at risk.

ifSOC2ObservationPeriodFails.note: RE-FRAMED per DR-014. The risk is no longer 'will 100 controls get built' — they were, by Jul 15, and Deloitte accepted the evidence Aug 7. The risk is now control DRIFT during the Sep 1 – Nov 30 observation window: a control that stops operating cleanly restarts its clock and moves the Dec 15 report into FY2027, taking Meridian Financial ($4.2M), Nuvera ($2.1M), and three expansion tracks with it. Note that $6.3M of this already moved from Q3 to Q4 as a timing consequence of the restatement — that is a slipped quarter, not lost revenue.

ifHorizonAppStoreReviewFails.note: Kestrel tranche 1 ($800K) RELEASED Jul 15 — removed from risk. Remaining exposure: Solaris ($2.4M, Sep 15) and Kestrel tranche 2 ($800K, Oct), both gated on public App Store GA Aug 31. Soft GA landed on time Jul 31, so the delivery risk is closed; what remains is an Apple review decision expected Aug 15-22 that NovaGrid does not control. A rejection requiring resubmission is the scenario that puts $3.2M back in play.

ifAtlasUptimeRegresses.note: RE-FRAMED. Launch risk is gone — GA shipped Jun 30 with 3 enterprise customers in production. The live risk is operational: rolling uptime fell to 96.8% on Jul 6 under GA load and was only recovered by rate-limiting onboarding (DR-011) until the F6 circuit breaker shipped Jul 31. Uptime is 98.9% and holding, but the 99.0% July commitment was missed. Apex Health is a healthcare customer in production. A second visible breach costs more than the first, because the first was disclosed proactively and the second would look like a pattern.

ifSparkM2Slips.note: VantagePoint renewal CLOSED WON Jul 15 — the $1.8M is banked, not at risk this year. What is exposed is the Sep 15 contractual roadmap review, which expects M2 (model serving alpha) to have closed. M2 sits at 88% against an Aug 11 target with go/no-go today. A 1-2 week slip still clears Sep 15; a longer one turns a satisfied renewal into a difficult FY2027 negotiation.
